title: ViewSwitcher
wrapsNative: MonarchSegmentedControl, one titled segment with an SF Symbol per view (a SwiftUI segmented Picker draws a title or an image, never both)
summary: A recipe, not a component: a segmented Picker that switches one data set between table, board, calendar and gallery views.
whenToUse: Above a collection that can be shown in two to five layouts, when the choice applies at once and stays while the person works.
whenNotToUse: For more than five views, or views that are separate screens, use a Menu in the toolbar or a TabView. For filters, use MonarchTag with a selection.
api: Picker(_ title: String, selection: Binding<SelectionValue>, content: () -> Content).pickerStyle(.segmented)

states.name: disabled
states.description: disabled(_:) on the Picker disables every segment; there is no per-segment disabled state in the segmented style.

appearance: The system segmented control in every theme. Text segments use the system font of the control; icon segments use SF Symbols chosen for each view.
platformNotes: The web ViewSwitcher is a SegmentedControl with built-in labels and icons for table, board, calendar, gallery, list and timeline, counts after the labels, sizes, and labels that hide on narrow screens. On iOS a segmented Picker already does the switching; each segment shows a text or an image, not both, so the recipe chooses text when the labels fit and icons named for VoiceOver when they do not. The app supplies the names and symbols, so Monarch ships no strings for them. Android shares the recipe approach.
accessibility: System behaviour: the control is read as a group of segments with the selected one marked.
Icon segments need accessibilityLabel on each Image, so VoiceOver reads the view's name instead of the symbol name.
The Picker's title ("View") names the group.
edgeCases: At the largest text sizes, long text segments are shortened by the system; switch to icons or a Menu when they no longer fit.
Keep the chosen view in the app's state (for example AppStorage) so it survives a relaunch.

examples.title: Default views
examples.template:
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
    MonarchSegmentedControl(
        "View",
        selection: $mode,
        items: [
            MonarchSegmentedItem({{views.0.label}}, value: {{views.0.value}}, systemImage: "tablecells"),
            MonarchSegmentedItem({{views.1.label}}, value: {{views.1.value}}, systemImage: "rectangle.split.3x1"),
            MonarchSegmentedItem({{views.2.label}}, value: {{views.2.value}}, systemImage: "calendar"),
            MonarchSegmentedItem({{views.3.label}}, value: {{views.3.value}}, systemImage: "square.grid.2x2"),
        ],
        size: .xs,
        fillsWidth: false
    )
    Text("Showing the " + mode + " view.")
        .monarchTextStyle(.body)
}
